passage.title: 简·爱
passage.author: Charlotte Bronte
passage.text: To tell me that I had already a wife is empty mockery: you know now that I had but a hideous demon. I was wrong to attempt to deceive you; but I feared a stubbornness that exists in your character. I feared early instilled prejudice: I wanted to have you safe before hazarding confidences. Not a human being that ever lived could wish to be loved better than I was loved; and him who thus loved me I absolutely worshipped: and I must renounce love and idol. For a wife I have but the maniac upstairs: as well might you refer me to some corpse in yonder churchyard. And what a distortion in your judgment, what a perversity in your ideas, is proved by your conduct! Is it better to drive a fellow-creature to despair than to transgress a mere human law, no man being injured by the breach?

q.t: He was brought from the castle by Szgany, and probably they delivered their cargo to Slovaks who took the boxes to Varna, for there they were shipped for London.

words.m: n. 色淀；湖泊, 湖畔

q.t: Across Marsh, Tagish, and Bennett (seventy miles of lakes), they flew so fast that the man whose turn it was to run towed behind the sled at the end of a rope.

words.m: a. 不像的, 不同的 prep. 不像, 和...不同

o.t: Not at all—I never saw him; but I fancy he is very unlike his brother—silly and a great coxcomb.

q.t: Your being so far unlike, Fanny, does not in the smallest degree make against the probability of your happiness together: do not imagine it.

words.m: pl. 老鼠

o.t: Near villages and small towns I have found the nests of humble-bees more numerous than elsewhere, which I attribute to the number of cats that destroy the mice.

q.t: I heard the mice too, rattling behind the panels, as if the same occurrence were important to their interests.

b.t: Wherefore ye shall make images of your emerods, and images of your mice that mar the land; and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel: peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.

words.m: n. 名望, 名声, 传说

q.t: He would have had his Erin famed, The green flag gloriously unfurled, Her statesmen, bards and warriors raised Before the nations of the World.

b.t: And the fame thereof was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, Joseph’s brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
